summary: Only one of the eight claimed workflows is actually depicted: every action and complete screenshot in this set renders the same 'Club board / Board 1 / Round 3 / 12 players / Ava vs Liam / Ava wins 1-0' match-result detail. Six workflows (rankings-table, club-night, pairing-queue, export-package, rules-documents, discussion-thread) share byte-identical action and complete captures under a generic 'Chess Club home' title, and the meetup workflow reuses the match-result captures verbatim under 'Board 1 match result' — so there is no rankings table, no calendar, no queue detail, no export payload, no document list, and no discussion thread anywhere in the evidence. The complete state always announces 'Chess result saved' regardless of workflow, and every minimized card carries the identical four-button shell (Tap for expanded view / Member form / Expand / Record match result), so 'Record match result' is offered as the primary CTA on rules-documents and discussion cards. Copy across the set is rubric-restating rather than product copy ('Member form captures labeled details, privacy c…', 'Ad preference and sponsored-message beh…', 'In-focus product surface', 'Choice and standing'), and start screens are captured mid-scroll with clipped headers and titles.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Across this community's workflows, is it always clear what workflow and what state (start/in-progress/complete) the user is looking at?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: No. State is somewhat legible — the complete screens carry a distinct 'Chess result saved' banner plus a 'Club record' history block, and the start screens show status chips like 'Waiting', 'Not available' and 'Saved' — but workflow identity collapses almost entirely. Six workflows' action screens are the same image titled 'Chess Club home' showing the Board 1 / Ava vs Liam match result, and the meetup workflow's action screen is the match-result screen titled 'Board 1 match result'. A user on the rankings, calendar, export, rules or discussion workflow would see a chess match score and nothing identifying the workflow they opened. The complete banner compounds it by saying 'Chess result saved' even on the export-package and rules-documents runs.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the displayed text read like real product copy about actual Chess Club content, or like generic/spec-restating placeholder?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: Mixed, trending placeholder. A thin layer of genuinely chess-specific copy exists — 'Ava vs Liam, Board 1, friendly ladder night', 'Ava wins 1-0; standings and next pairing will update', 'Board 1', 'Round 3', '12 players' — and it reads like a real club. But it is surrounded by copy that restates the acceptance criteria instead of describing content: 'Confirm player names, round, board, result, edit option, and standings update before saving.', 'Choice and standing — Nominations, ballot options, selected title, match result, or standings are visible before saving.', 'Member form captures labeled details, privacy c…', 'Ad preference and sponsored-message beh…', 'In-focus product surface', 'Local package details', and 'The saved result keeps status, history, and change actions visible for this community task.' Card subtitles are also mismatched: the 'Pairing discussion' card is subtitled with ad-preference text.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Are the available actions clear, and is it clear why disabled or unavailable ones are unavailable?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: No. The same action set is stamped onto every card regardless of what the card is: 'Tap for expanded view', 'Member form', 'Expand', and 'Record match result' appear on the 'Club night calendar', 'Rules documents', 'Pairing discussion' and 'Organizer pairing queue' cards, where recording a match result is not a sensible action. Unavailability is asserted without a reason a legacy-schema user could act on: 'Not available' paired with 'Another community role manages this item.' names no role and offers no path. The 'Waiting' chip on chess-match-meetup_start at least explains itself ('Waiting for the member form to be submitted.'). On chess-export-package_start the primary button carries a download icon but is still labeled 'Record match result', so icon and label disagree outright.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the visual presentation free of repeated generic card shells, clipping, crowding and empty content where real content is expected?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: No. Every start screen is a stack of visually interchangeable dark card shells with the same icon (clipboard), the same 'Minimized' chip on the right, and the same two rows of four buttons; only the title line differs, and titles truncate ('Organizer pairing que…'). Start screens are captured mid-scroll so headers are clipped — chess-match-meetup_start opens with 'Club board' sliced by the app bar, and card content is cut off behind the bottom navigation on nearly every start capture. The action/complete sheets also cut off below 'Standings — Players can see updated ladder position and next match.' with two button shells half-visible behind the nav bar. The brown-on-brown treatment of the complete sheet gives low contrast between the 'Club board' card and its container.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does what is shown make sense for the specific workflow being demonstrated on each row?
holisticQuestionAnswers.answer: No, for six of eight workflows it is outright wrong. The rankings-table, club-night, pairing-queue, export-package, rules-documents and discussion-thread rows all resolve to a chess match-result detail. There is no ranked ladder table, no dated club-night calendar entries, no queue of waiting players, no export file/size/format, no document list with titles or versions, and no thread with messages or authors anywhere in the 24 captures. The bottom nav offers Matches, Calendar and Rankings tabs, but 'Home' remains the selected tab on every single screen, including the two rows that are supposed to be demonstrating the rankings table and the club night calendar.

findings.title: Six workflows' action and complete states are the same match-result screen
findings.description: The action captures for chess-rankings-table, chess-club-night, chess-pairing-queue, chess-export-package, chess-rules-documents and chess-discussion-thread are byte-identical (hash e0033376…), and their complete captures are likewise byte-identical (hash 0c88ea55…). All twelve render the same content: heading 'Chess Club home', chips 'Board 1', 'Round 3', '12 players', 'Correction option', 'Players — Ava vs Liam, Board 1, friendly ladder night.', 'Result — Ava wins 1-0; standings and next pairing will update.', and the actions 'Edit score', 'Dispute result', 'Open standings'. No rankings table, calendar, queue, export artifact, document, or thread appears anywhere in the set. Six of eight workflows therefore have no evidence of their own behaviour.
findings.requiredFix: Each workflow must render and be captured showing its own subject matter: a ranked ladder for rankings-table, dated club-night entries for club-night, an ordered waiting list for pairing-queue, a named export artifact for export-package, a document list/body for rules-documents, and authored posts for discussion-thread — each with a workflow-specific title rather than 'Chess Club home'.

findings.title: chess-match-meetup action and complete are the chess-match-result captures
findings.description: chess-match-meetup_action is pixel-identical to chess-match-result_action (hash 492aa15c…) and chess-match-meetup_complete is pixel-identical to chess-match-result_complete (hash 845b7a08…). Both are titled 'Board 1 match result' and show a concluded score ('Ava wins 1-0'), with the complete state banner reading 'Chess result saved'. A meetup workflow — arranging when and where a game happens — is never depicted; there is no date, time, venue, invitation or confirmation anywhere in the three meetup rows.
findings.requiredFix: Build and capture a real meetup surface: proposed opponent, date/time, board and venue, with propose/accept/reschedule actions and a completion that confirms the scheduled game rather than a saved score.

findings.title: Every complete state announces 'Chess result saved' regardless of workflow
findings.description: All eight workflows' complete captures display the banner 'Chess result saved — Chess Club shows board, players, result, correction option, standings impact, and next pairing.' On the export-package, rules-documents and discussion-thread rows this actively misinforms: the user is told a chess score was saved when they exported a package, updated a document, or posted a message. The supporting card compounds it with 'The saved result keeps status, history, and change actions visible for this community task.', where 'this community task' is a generic stand-in for the thing the user actually did.
findings.requiredFix: Derive the completion banner from the workflow that completed and name the concrete object — e.g. 'Rankings published', 'Club night scheduled for Thu 14 Aug', 'chess-club-results.csv ready', 'Club rules v3 saved', 'Reply posted' — and drop the 'this community task' placeholder.

findings.title: 'Record match result' is the CTA on unrelated cards, and its icon contradicts its label on export
findings.description: Every minimized card in this community carries the identical four-button shell — 'Tap for expanded view', 'Member form', 'Expand', 'Record match result' — regardless of the card's subject. It appears on 'Club night calendar', 'Rules documents', 'Pairing discussion' and 'Organizer pairing queue' cards, where recording a chess score is not a valid action. On chess-export-package_start the same full-width button renders a download/export glyph while still reading 'Record match result', so the icon and label describe different actions.
findings.requiredFix: Give each card the action that belongs to its own content type ('Open rules', 'Reply', 'RSVP', 'Export', 'View queue') and make the button icon match its label everywhere.

findings.title: Body copy restates acceptance criteria and is mismatched to its cards
findings.description: Across the set, copy describes mechanisms rather than content: 'Confirm player names, round, board, result, edit option, and standings update before saving.', 'Choice and standing — Nominations, ballot options, selected title, match result, or standings are visible before saving.', 'Open result — Change vote, dispute score, view results, and next meeting or round stay available.', 'Member form captures labeled details, privacy c…', and the engine-jargon strips 'In-focus product surface' and 'Local package details'. Ballot and nomination vocabulary appears in a chess community that has no voting workflow. Worse, on chess-rankings-table_start the card titled 'Pairing discussion' is subtitled 'Ad preference and sponsored-message beh…', which is advertising-consent copy on a chess pairing card.
findings.requiredFix: Replace criteria-restating and cross-domain copy with sentences describing the actual chess content on each card, and remove internal strings like 'In-focus product surface' and 'Local package details' from user-visible surfaces.

findings.title: Clipped headers, truncated titles, actions cut by the nav bar, and duplicate 'Club board' headings
findings.description: Start captures are mid-scroll with the leading card header sliced by the app bar (chess-match-meetup_start, chess-match-result_start). Titles and subtitles truncate mid-word ('Organizer pairing que…', 'Member form captures labeled details, privacy c…'). On chess-rules-documents_start a 'Member tools' heading is cut to unreadable glyph tops behind the bottom nav. Every complete sheet cuts two follow-up buttons in half behind the Home/Matches/Calendar/Rankings bar, so the terminal state offers no reachable next step. Separately, chess-club-night_start, chess-pairing-queue_start, chess-export-package_start, chess-rules-documents_start and chess-discussion-thread_start each stack two sibling cards both titled 'Club board', destroying hierarchy, and the brown-on-brown sheet gives the inner card almost no edge contrast.
findings.requiredFix: Add bottom padding so sheet actions clear the navigation bar, capture start states from the top of the scroll, allow card titles to wrap to two lines instead of ellipsizing, deduplicate the sibling 'Club board' headings, and raise card-versus-sheet contrast in the brown theme.

findings.title: 'Not available' cards cite an unnamed role and still offer a form button
findings.description: On chess-match-result_start, the 'Live rankings table' and 'Club night calendar' cards each show a 'Not available' chip beside the identical sentence 'Another community role manages this item.' No role is named and no path to request access is offered, so the restriction is an unexplained dead end — particularly in this legacy schema where there is no identity or role display to reconcile it against. Both cards simultaneously present a 'Member form' button while marked not available, which contradicts the chip.
findings.requiredFix: Name the managing role concretely (e.g. 'Managed by the club organizer') and either hide or visibly disable the secondary buttons on cards marked 'Not available' so the affordances agree with the state.

findings.title: 'Home' stays the selected nav tab on all 24 screens, including the rankings and calendar workflows
findings.description: The bottom navigation offers Home, Matches, Calendar and Rankings, and the 'Home' pill is rendered as the filled/selected tab on every one of the 24 captures — including chess-rankings-table_start/action/complete and chess-club-night_start/action/complete, whose workflows correspond directly to the Rankings and Calendar tabs. On chess-match-meetup_start and chess-rankings-table_start the 'Rankings' pill is additionally clipped by the right screen edge.
findings.requiredFix: Select the nav tab that corresponds to the surface being shown, and size the tab row so the fourth pill is not clipped at the right edge.
